title: Stage 3: Fit
summary: Hold out test houses with a seeded split, then fit a linear regression with least squares.

steps.title: Stage 3: hold out, then fit
body: A model graded on the houses it learned from will look better than it is. So first **set aside** some houses it never sees:
idx = np.random.default_rng(42).permutation(n)   # shuffled 0..n-1, same every run
Then **least squares** finds the coefficients `b` that make `X @ b` as close as possible to `y` (smallest sum of squared errors):
`lstsq` returns four things; you only need the first.

steps.prompt: Why shuffle before splitting instead of taking the first 80% of rows?
options: Rows may be ordered (by date, area, price), so the first 80% may not look like the rest
Shuffling makes the model more accurate on training data
It does not matter at all

steps.explain: The data lie exactly on `y = 3 + 2x`, so least squares recovers intercept 3 and slope 2, and predictions match exactly.

steps.title: A seeded split
prompt: - the test set has `round(n * test_frac)` indexes, taken from the **end** of the shuffled order; the rest (from the start) are training.
For `n=36` that is 29 training and 7 test houses, and the test indexes are `[11, 14, 34, 2, 1, 13, 8]`.

105,3,2016,Hilltop,308
154,4,2010,Hilltop,448
186,5,1955,Hilltop,462
160,3,1970,Central,439
"""


def load(text):
    return pd.read_csv(io.StringIO(text))


def price_correlations(df):
    corr = df.corr(numeric_only=True)["price"].drop("price")
    return corr.sort_values(ascending=False).round(2)


def plot_size_vs_price(df):
    fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(6, 4))
    ax.scatter(df["sqm"], df["price"])
    ax.set_title("Price vs size")
    ax.set_xlabel("Size (sqm)")
    ax.set_ylabel("Price ($k)")
    return fig


FEATURES = ["sqm", "bedrooms", "age", "nb_Hilltop", "nb_Riverside"]


def add_features(df):
    out = df.copy()
    out["age"] = 2024 - out["year_built"]
    dummies = pd.get_dummies(out["neighbourhood"], prefix="nb", drop_first=True, dtype=int)
    return pd.concat([out.drop(columns=["year_built", "neighbourhood"]), dummies], axis=1)


def make_xy(df, features):
    X = np.column_stack([np.ones(len(df)), df[features].to_numpy(dtype=float)])
    y = df["price"].to_numpy(dtype=float)
    return X, y


def split(n, test_frac=0.2, seed=42):
    idx = np.random.default_rng(seed).permutation(n)
    n_train = n - round(n * test_frac)
    return idx[:n_train], idx[n_train:]


def main():
    df = add_features(load(RAW))
    X, y = make_xy(df, FEATURES)
    print(X.shape, y.shape)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
